newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Dutch U.N. police monitor wounded in Bosnia.
newsitem.headline: Dutch U.N. police monitor wounded in Bosnia.

text.p: A Dutch U.N. police monitor was wounded by gunfire in the northeast Bosnian town of Koraj on Monday during disturbances between Moslems and Serbs, a United Nations spokesman said.

A crowd of Serbs fired shots to prevent about Moslem refugees returning to their homes across an ethnic boundary line in Bosnia and NATO-led peacekeeping forces sealed off the area, Alex Ivanko, a U.N. police spokesman said.
"One of our Dutch police monitors was wounded in Koraj this morning," said U.N. spokesman Andrea Angelli, speaking to Reuters by telephone from Tuzla.
"The bullet came from the weapon of a Serb policeman. We are not in a position to say if it was a direct (intentional) shot or not but he (the Dutch monitor) still has the bullet in his body."
Angelli said the Dutchman had been evacuated by Russian soldiers deployed in Bosnia as part of a NATO-led peacekeeping force.
Trouble broke out in Koraj early on Monday when as many as 500 Moslems attempted to return to their former homes in the nearby Serb-held village of Gajevi, northeast of Tuzla.
The Inter-Entity Boundary Line (IEBL) was established under Bosnia's Dayton peace accord to distinguish Serb-held territory from that controlled by Moslems and Croats.
The line was intended to be an administrative boundary but has hardened into a de facto border.

Ivanko said a number of Moslems had applied to return to homes in the village of Gajevi on the Serb side of the IEBL from which they were driven or fled during the Bosnian war and that those trying to cross at Koraj on Monday were among them.
Gajevi is located in northeastern Bosnia, and northeast of the city of Tuzla.
The U.N. police spokesman said the review and approval process for the Moslem applications to return to Gajevi had not yet been completed. Their move was premature under currently agreed procedures.
Moslems returning to villages along the IEBL east of Tuzla sparked violence on several occasions this year, as did some attempted IEBL crossings by Moslems intent on visiting their former homes.
